facts.text: Hueytown takes its name from the Huey family, early settlers who followed the first land claim by William Brown in 1815.
In 1815, William Brown left Tennessee and founded what later became known as “Possum Valley,” the seed of Hueytown.
Virginia Mines, opened in 1902, remains one of the first coal mines in Hueytown, with its original buildings still listed on the Alabama Register of Historic Places.
An underground explosion in Hueytown’s mines became one of Alabama’s worst disasters, entombing an entire day crew.
Hueytown Public Library opened in 1969 within a municipal hallway before moving into its own building in 1990.
Hueytown High School’s marching band has earned regional prestige, performing alongside the University of Alabama at Birmingham’s symphonic ensembles.
